slots.title: ISM services PMI 55.4 beats 54.3 estimate
slots.body:
August ISM Services PMI: **55.4** (forecast **54.3**, prior **54.1**).

That keeps the headline gauge in expansion territory — anything above 50 means more firms reporting growth than shrinkage in services, which cover most of U.S. jobs outside factories.

New orders: **60.9** vs **57.0** expected.

Prices paid: **72.6** vs **66.0** expected (prior **70.3**).

Employment subindex: **47.8** vs **51.8** expected — still below 50, so more respondents reported fewer hires than more.

Business activity: **61.7** vs **59.0** expected.

Which subindex — orders, prices, or hiring — matters most to you ahead of tomorrow’s payroll report?

slots.title: Jobless claims 206K; continuing claims 1.779M
slots.body:

Initial claims count people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time; continuing claims count those still on benefits — both are weekly inputs before the monthly jobs report.

slots.title: US Cash Session Recap — Sept. 3, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equities closed higher across the major benchmarks: the S&P 500 finished at 7,748.27 (+1.1%), the Nasdaq Composite at 26,584.06 (+1.4%), and the Dow at 53,686.11 (+624.16 points, +1.2%).
The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% to 2,968.27.
Headlines in the feed linked the move to Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s comment that he could support holding rates steady.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell to 14.32, down 5.8% on the day, while session ranges showed the S&P traded between 7,686.71 and 7,756.76.

On the calendar, ISM Services PMI for August printed at 55.4 vs a 54.3 estimate (above 50 means expansion in that survey).
ISM Services New Orders was 60.9, and ISM Services Prices was 72.6.
Initial jobless claims for the Aug. 29 week were 206K vs a 205K estimate; continuing claims were 1,779K.
Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 was updated to 4.7% vs 4.8% prior.

Nasdaq sector averages in the data showed Industrials up 3.3%, Real Estate up 1.8%, Financial Services up 1.7%, and Technology up 1.0%.
Utilities (-1.2%) and Basic Materials (-1.2%) lagged, and Healthcare was down 0.6% on average.

Megacap tech was mixed:
- $MSFT +2.7% to 510.12
- $GOOGL +1.6% to 342.48
- $AMZN +1.5% to 258.90
- $NVDA +1.8% to 228.45

while $AVGO closed -2.7% at 357.16.
$ORCL stood out among large software names at +5.7% (154.04).

Earnings drove several large single-name moves.
$CIEN reported EPS of 2.11 on revenue of $1.67B (both above estimates) but finished -10.4% at 317.46.
$ZS rose 2.9% after EPS of 1.19 vs 1.09 estimated; $IOT gained 5.3% on a 0.20 vs 0.16 EPS print; $GWRE rose 5.2%.
$CPB fell 7.0% despite EPS roughly in line with estimates; $VSXY dropped 13.2% with EPS 0.95 vs 0.774 estimated; $TTC was down 6.8% after reporting.

Cross-asset reads from the injected tape: gold futures (GCUSD) at 4,517.10 (-0.5%), the United States Oil Fund (USO) at 142.09 (+0.7%), Brent crude (BZUSD) near flat at 95.94, the dollar proxy UUP at 28.01 (-0.6%), and Bitcoin at 80,797.48 (-0.6%).

Treasury snapshot dated Sept. 1 in the data showed the 10-year yield at 4.8% and the 2s10s spread at 0.40 percentage point.

Overseas indexes in the feed included Hang Seng +2.2% to 25,767.00, Nikkei 225 +0.9%, and FTSE 100 +0.7%.
